sentence: This project builds a toolkit that classifies small fossil fish teeth and shark scales, then studies how fish responded to major environmental events.
This project builds a system using small molecules to control how much a gene is used in mammalian cells, instead of turning it on or off.
This project turns poultry litter into biochar hydrogel materials and tests how well they remove per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances from water and soil.
This project uses phospho-proteomics to find signaling pathways that help white blood cells attack tumor cells.
This project tests whether heat-assisted desiccation can preserve microbial samples in remote regions well enough to yield suitable DNA for sequencing.
This project studies how human driver preferences and automated vehicles shape each other and traffic, to find a balance between driver needs and traffic flow.
This project develops computer methods that learn which statistical measures of a material's internal structure matter most for its physical properties.
This project develops inequalities for integral transformations and uses them to study whether averages over repeated evolution of dynamical systems converge.
This project builds a framework to study how imperfect optical hardware and unpredictable environmental noise affect the reliability of snapshot compressive imaging.
This project develops a way for organizations to ask each other targeted queries about their operational states for intrusion detection, while protecting operational privacy.
This project holds a conference where statisticians, scientists and legal and forensic professionals discuss data-based ways to evaluate forensic evidence.
This project studies how the hormone prolactin relates to parental care in birds that leave their eggs in the nests of other species.
This project tests whether mixotrophic algae, which use photosynthesis and ingest prey, help copepods reproduce when algal food is of poor quality.
This project holds a conference where researchers share advances in the molecular biology of bacteria and phages.
This project develops a sensor that detects phosphorus in water using electrodes modified with a nanocomposite material.
This project improves the data that graph neural networks learn from, making it more compact, cleaner and better aligned with learning objectives.
